summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update35.json → valid=true). New finding on the transport configuration surface, graded as an API/documentation gap with an operational effect. The install-snapshot path is the one place where a large, slow transfer must fit inside a deadline, and that deadline is computed as the transport timeout multiplied by snapshot size divided by a named factor (net_transport.go:515-522). The timeout field's documentation names that factor as though it belonged to the configuration (161-163), but the configuration struct declares no such field — it ends after the message-pack option (164-170) — while the name exists only as an exported integer on the transport struct itself (109-113), which the constructor unconditionally overwrites with the package default (221-238). So a caller following the documented configuration path finds no knob, and a caller who sets the field afterwards is mutating a live transport outside any documented path; the remaining documented lever is raising the transport timeout, which is also the deadline for every other RPC (the generic path sets each connection's deadline from it), so accommodating snapshots that way also lengthens the deadlines that bound votes, appends and heartbeats. Recorded as one Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation with the discriminator stated (set the documented name and observe no change), and counterevidence kept honest: the exported field means tuning is not impossible, only undocumented and awkward to set safely; the default is reasonable for ordinary transfers so the gap only bites deployments near the deadline; raising the timeout is not wrong for a slow link, the objection being that it also governs unrelated RPCs; and nothing was measured — the record is explicitly operational/API rather than a protocol-correctness claim.
